newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE SHARES SPOOKED BY DUAL LISTING ALARM.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE SHARES SPOOKED BY DUAL LISTING ALARM.

text.p: Fears over the possible termination of dual listings in 16 blue chips including the Big Four banks jolted Singapore shares to a mixed close on Friday.

"The possible delisting of foreign tranches was foremost in the minds of investors. There was a lot of uncertainties and confusion over the issue and that worsened sentiment," said a dealer with a local bank.

ST Computer Systems & Services Ltd's move to merge its two tranches from Friday set off a buzz of speculation over whether companies like Singapore Airlines (SIA) and Singapore Press Holdings Ltd (SPH) would follow suit.
A Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) statement in the late morning that it had no intention to ask banks to merge the tranches helped stabilise the market, dealers said.
ST Computer ended Singapore $0.05 up at S$1.06. SPH foreign ended off its low at S$26.40, down S$0.80 while its local tranche ended S$0.40 down at S$12.90.
DBS Bank foreign shed S$0.70 to S$17.40 while its local shares rose 10 cents to S$9.50.
HK Land Holdings topped the actives with over 11.2 million shares. It ended unchanged at US$3.42.
The Straits Times Industrials Index ended 9.32 points down at 1,943.92.
